backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (~262K tokens/step). With a fixed 300 s budget, more optimizer steps usually help small models. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so grad accumulation halves automatically. Check that the assertion on divisibility still holds.

backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 for the Muon params.

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSSL" or "SSL" variant. Try "SSL" for more full-attention layers, or "SSSSSSSL" for fewer, to trade compute for quality. Pick "SSSSSSSL" for speed.
backlog.title: Window pattern all-short plus last long

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 so there are twice as many attention heads. Check that the kv-head count handling in the config still works.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Reduce the MLP hidden size from 4x to 3x model_dim (the c_fc and c_proj shapes). This gives faster steps and more tokens in 300 s. Keep init the same.
backlog.title: Squared-ReLU to SwiGLU-free tweak: MLP expansion 3x

backlog.spec: Lower the logit softcap constant (likely 15) to 12, or raise it to 30 if it's already low. Edit the single constant in the forward pass.

backlog.spec: Zero-initialize the attention c_proj and MLP c_proj weights if they are not already, so each block starts as the identity.

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step, after the final micro-batch backward. This stabilizes a higher LR.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 128 to maximize occupied memory before overflow. Add a soft gradient accumulation loop of 2 steps (128e+128) to keep total step frequency similar but improve discretization accuracy, effectively halving the effective batch per step to 131K while better utilizing the GPU.
backlog.title: Double the device batch size with gradient accumulation

backlog.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO = 32 and keep DEPTH at 6. This reduces model_dim to 256, cutting embedding and matrix costs by ~25% while increasing head count. This is a state-space compression that mimics larger models with lower memory and allows smaller steps.
backlog.title: Reduce ASPECT_RATIO to 32 at fixed depth

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.2 instead of 0.0. This keeps the learning rate elevated longer, enabling more gradient updates per wall-clock era to settle the optimizer step at a lower effective loss, which typically reduces val_bpb.

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.90, 0.95). A lower beta1 reduces the memory of the running average of gradients, allowing the optimizer to respond more quickly to early gradient shifts in a short-evaluation window.
backlog.title: Reduce Adam beta1 to 0.90

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.5. This acts as a strength regularization term for the moment terms in Muon, typically stabilizing the low-resolution, noisy training needed for a short wall-clock era.
backlog.title: Increase weight decay from 0.2 to 0.5

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSS' (all half-length) with windowed scaled attention. This constrains the model to focus on previous tokens less and recent history more, which often improves the smoothness of the prediction in short training windows.
backlog.title: Split window pattern into shorter contexts

backlog.spec: Set MATRIX_LR = 0.08 instead of 0.04. This increases the effective update size per step for the dense layers, compensating for the shallower step size achieved by the smaller batch per step.
backlog.title: Increase matrix LR to 0.08

backlog.spec: Increase the ratio of the attention heads to the output size (or similar expansion) to widen the internal layers, allowing the model to capture more representational fidelity per parameter for a larger step count with similar memory.
backlog.title: Expand MLP by merging internal hidden dimensions

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0 (or a very small value like 0.01 if already cold). Since schedule tweaking was previously out of distribution, starting immediately at the peak learning rate can be superior when wall-clock time is tight.
backlog.title: Reduce WARMUP_RATIO to 0.0

backlog.spec: Modify the schedule to end linear warmdown earlier by halving the FINAL_LR_FRAC or adjusting the buffer to exponentiate with a steeper slope, effectively reducing variance in updates at the end of the training period.
backlog.title: Tighten LR schedule with stricter logarithmic decay

backlog.spec: Apply per-token dropout to the pre-attention and post-attention output projections with rate 0.05 to simplify decision boundaries and reduce overfitting.
backlog.title: Coupled Attention Dropouts

backlog.spec: Replace linear warmup with a stepped schedule: warm for the first 10% of the budget at 0.7*initial_lr, then decay linearly over the remaining 90%.
backlog.title: Adaptive Step Size Annealing

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH=6 but split the 128/head-vec dimension into 64 heads layers 1-3 and 32 heads layers 4-6. Actually set DEPTH=7 to make this work without changing ASPECT_RATIO.
backlog.title: Depth-Dependent Head Split

backlog.spec: Modifiy init weights so that the residual projection c_proj is initialized with a scaled Gaussian (1.0 + 0.3 * eps) instead of zero-mean to boost gradient flow early.
backlog.title: Lambda-init Residuals

backlog.spec: Change sliding window stride from 2 to 4 tokens, reducing causal context per step to 40-60 tokens for faster convergence without large parameter changes.
backlog.title: Sliding Window Stride 4

backlog.spec: Apply a logit clipping function with bound 0.7 * log(e_max) to limit output magnitudes, reducing numerical instability and forcing cleaner convergence.
backlog.title: Logit Softcap with 0.7z

backlog.spec: Use an Exponential Moving Average of parameters for the optimizer with alpha=0.95 to reduce noise and improve generalization.
backlog.title: Optimal Moving Average EMA

backlog.spec: Replace the currently linear warmup scheme with a steep initial spike followed by linear decay to 10% of the initial learning rate.
backlog.title: Linear Decay to 10% LR

backlog.spec: Switch to a no-padding dependency scheme where each transformer block input length depends on previous input length, reducing memory overhead.
backlog.title: Reduced Padding Migration

backlog.spec: Apply weight decay to all parameters except embedding and LM head parameters, for a stricter regularization regime.
backlog.title: AdamW with AdamW-compatible Weight Decay

memo:
Helped: structural changes that fit the fixed 300 s budget. Depth 8 to 6 gave 1.0834/1.0875 (delta -0.0291, accepted). TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE ~262K gave 1.0658/1.0664 (delta -0.0193, accepted). Both carry a tripwire flag, so verify them before trusting the gains. Incumbent is 1.0661 over 2 runs.

Promising but rejected: batch 2^17 (~131K) gave 1.0618 (-0.0044), the best single result so far. It was rejected, probably because it was a single run, so it deserves a replicate or a retry.

Did not help: DEPTH 10 (1.1652, +0.0798), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0040), MATRIX_LR 0.08 (+0.0006), 0.05 (+0.0000), weight decay 0.5 (+0.0022), LR spike (+0.0016). Schedule and regularization tweaks were near noise: warmdown 0.7 (-0.0001), weight decay 0.1 (-0.0003), warmup (-0.0016), clipping (-0.0005).

Next: replicate or push the batch size lower, try depth 5 and other widths at depth 6, then retune LR for the new batch. Stop tuning schedule and regularization.
